root_cause_label: Strategic Diversion into Fake Checkpoint I/O Debugging Loop
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent abandoned the real task at step 8 to build and debug a fake binary checkpoint format, spending 20+ steps in a fruitless I/O loop before giving up without ever attempting the GPT-2 transformer or BPE tokenizer.
t_err_evidence: At step 8, the agent writes generate_ckpt.c to create a 'fake.ckpt' with a self-invented binary format (fixed string header + tensor name length + tensor data), acting on the false premise that this fake checkpoint is a useful proxy for the actual TensorFlow checkpoint format. This strategic diversion — building a toy I/O exercise instead of approaching the real task — is the decisive mistake.
t_commit_evidence: From step 8 onward the agent is entirely consumed by generating, writing, and debugging the fake checkpoint read/write loop; it never returns to the actual GPT-2 weights, BPE tokenizer, or the 5000-byte constraint, making failure inevitable from this point.
t_surface_evidence: Step 13 shows the first observable failure signal: running gpt2.c against fake.ckpt produces 'Tensor name: ' and 'Tensor value: 0.000000', indicating the binary parsing logic is completely broken.
trigger_explanation: At step 8 the agent acts on the unverified assumption that inventing and parsing a custom binary checkpoint format is a valid path toward reading real TensorFlow checkpoint files. In reality the TF checkpoint format (protocol buffers + .index/.data shards) is entirely different from the agent's invented format, so the entire debugging effort is wasted on a fictional problem that has no relationship to the real task.
forewarning_evidence: Step 7 shows the agent reading random bytes from a /dev/urandom-seeded dummy .ckpt file and interpreting the hex dump as if it could reveal the real TF checkpoint structure. This signals the agent has no access to real model weights and is already working in a fictional context, but it proceeds to double down by creating the fake format generator.
fabrication_evidence: Starting at step 8 the agent fabricates a fake binary checkpoint format and an accompanying generator/parser, presenting this as progress toward GPT-2 inference. The fake format has no relation to real TensorFlow checkpoints. The agent spends steps 12-34 debugging trivial binary I/O within this fictional system, never engaging with the actual task requirements (real weights, BPE tokenizer, transformer forward pass, 5000-byte limit).
